name_reason: Name already matches the convention data_fd2_battle_<descriptor> for a battle-core global. 'ai_best_item_score' accurately describes the datum: enemy-AI best item-use candidate score, a signed scalar accumulator. No Ghidra address residue in the name. Consistent with the sibling result-group members data_fd2_battle_ai_best_item_slot/target_x/target_y and the parallel groups data_fd2_battle_ai_best_spell_score @0x53C23 / data_fd2_battle_ai_best_physical_score @0x53C4F.
purpose: Enemy-AI item-use scoring scratchpad: the best (highest) score found while enumerating every offensive inventory slot x every reachable target tile during one evaluation pass.
logic_summary: Signed int32 max-accumulator. fd2_ai_score_item_use inits it to 0 at entry (@0x1568F: MOV dword[0x53C33],0), then for each (slot,tile) candidate computes a score via fd2_score_item_candidate and, when score > current best (CMP @0x15800 then JLE @0x15806 = signed compare), stores it (@0x15808) together with the sibling outputs target_x @0x53C37, target_y @0x53C3B, slot_idx @0x53C3F. Read by fd2_attack_action_dispatch (@0x14F74..0x15022) and fd2_enemy_turn_phase_team0 (@0x1D936) where it is compared as a full signed dword against 0x6 and the sibling spell-score @0x53C23 / physical-score @0x53C4F to pick the winning AI action.
datatype: int32 (signed 4-byte). Ghidra type is still undefined4; src declares int32. Per refine-stage rules the datatype was NOT changed.
element_semantics: Single scalar score value (priority/score class produced by fd2_score_item_candidate). Higher is better; 0 means no usable item candidate. Threshold 6 distinguishes a 'good' item action from a fallback.
notes: Writers (game code) at 0x1568F (init 0) and 0x15808 (store best) => mutable runtime scratch state, NOT const. Memory @0x53C33 reads all-zero (zero-init BSS, .object2 segment). src comment (btl_aisc.c lines 646-658) was already accurate, concise, ASCII-clean, with no stale/phase content => kept; src not edited. Ghidra side: the descriptive comment existed in the deprecated PRE_COMMENT field while PLATE_COMMENT was null; per project_ghidra_data_plate_mechanism the data plate must live in PLATE_COMMENT, so the content (reflecting the src conclusion) was written to PLATE_COMMENT via run_script_inline and the misplaced PRE_COMMENT cleared (set_plate_via_java_api). Verified against disassembly of fd2_ai_score_item_use @0x1568F (JLE @0x15806 confirms signed compare; store sequence @0x15808/0x1580D/0x15816/0x1581F writes score/x/y/slot).
